name: AMD Instinct MI350P
memory_bandwidth_basis: '4 TB/s' per the AMD spec table on a 4096-bit interface - exactly half the 8192-bit MI350X/MI355X, with correspondingly half the memory (144GB vs 288GB). The page gives no memory-clock figure for this part, so the 4 TB/s is a vendor figure without published arithmetic. AUDIT CORRECTION: 4096-bit x 8 Gb/s per pin / 8 = 4,096 GB/s, not 4,000. The correct per-pin rate is 7.81 Gbps (4000 x 8 / 4096). (The generic 'HBM3E = 5.0 Gbps' assumption that a mechanical audit would apply gives 2,560 GB/s and is wrong for this part: MI350-series HBM3E runs at ~7.81 Gbps per pin, and AMD's own spec table lists 'Memory Clock 8 GHz'.)

flops.notes: AUDIT 2026-10-04: ROW ADDED, not corrected - FP64 was absent entirely. AMD's spec table prints 'Peak Double Precision (FP64) Performance 36.0 TFLOPs' and 'Peak Double Precision Matrix (FP64) Performance 36.0 TFLOPs' (vector and matrix paths identical on CDNA4). Recorded dense:true: AMD annotates sparsity only on rows it explicitly titles 'with Structured Sparsity' (FP8, FP16, BF16, INT8), and FP64 has no such row on any MI350-series page. Ratio check confirms the derivation: MI350X 72.1 and MI350P 36.0 are each exactly half MI355X's 78.6, matching the halved-XCD relationship between the parts (MI355X 8 XCDs at 2400 MHz, MI350X and MI350P 4 XCDs at 2200 MHz). This schema's precision enum has no fp64 member, hence precision 'other'.

notes:
AUDIT 2026-10-03 (AMD convention re-verified against the MI350P page; no values changed): the MI350P page uses the identical labelling scheme as the MI350X - 'Peak X Performance' DENSE, 'Peak X Performance with Structured Sparsity' SPARSE at 2x - so every dense flag here is correct. Same micro-scaling caveat as the MI350X: the MXFP4 and MXFP6 rows print 4.6 PFLOPs with NO sparsity variant and are therefore dense, not sparse-and-not-to-be-halved. This page also prints the vector-vs-matrix split explicitly ('Peak Half Precision (FP16) Performance 72 TFLOPs' against 'Peak Half Precision Matrix (FP16) Performance 1.15 PFLOPs'), and the record's two fp16 rows are those two different paths - 72.0 vector and 1150 matrix - now annotated so they cannot be read as a contradiction. THE POINT OF THIS PART for inference: it is the only CDNA4 part with a 4096-bit interface and a PCIe add-in-card form factor ('PCIe Add-in Card', 'Dimensions Full Height / Double Slot', 600W TBP configurable to 450W), i.e. it is the air-cooled, rack-optional MI350 member. Its 4 TB/s and 144 GB are exactly half the MI350X's 8 TB/s and 288 GB, and its dense matrix throughput is exactly half too - but it needs no OAM baseboard, which is often the binding constraint. The CDNA4 part you can actually buy as a normal add-in card, and the only CDNA4 SKU without an OAM/8-GPU-platform story. Exactly HALF of an OAM part in every dimension: 128 CUs vs 256, 8192 SPs vs 16,384, 512 matrix cores vs 1024, 73B transistors vs 185B, 144 GB vs 288 GB, 4096-bit vs 8192-bit, 4 TB/s vs 8 TB/s, 128 MB Infinity Cache vs 256 MB.

Note the page does NOT state a release year for MI350P (no 'Launch Date' field), so release_year 2025 is inferred from it shipping alongside the June 2025 MI350 series - treat it as approximate.

Power is the interesting part: 600W max TBP but 450W TBP is configurable, and the card uses a standard 12V-2x6 connector rather than a 54V UBB. That makes it deployable in ordinary air-cooled servers. Passive cooling, full height / 267mm / double slot, Linux x86_64 only.

No Infinity Fabric links are listed on the spec page - scale-up beyond the card is PCIe only. That is a real limitation for multi-GPU inference: the OAM parts get a 153 GB/s scale-up mesh, this card gets PCIe Gen5 x16 (128 GB/s bidirectional) per card.

CDNA4 software surface is confirmed on the product page: OpenMP, OpenCL, HIP, ROCm, TensorFlow, PyTorch, ONNX-RT, SGLang, JAX, Triton, Kokkos, RAJA. That is the broadest explicitly-listed framework support of any part here and worth noting for inference engine selection.

TF32 is software-emulated on CDNA4. Sparse figures are 2x dense. Two fp16 entries on purpose: 72 TFLOPS vector, 1150 TFLOPS matrix. MXFP6/MXFP4 at 4600 PFLOPs. ROCm LLVM target gfx950. FP64 (AUDIT 2026-10-04, row added): 36.0 TFLOPs, vector and matrix both, dense. Recorded on the sibling nvidia-b200 comparison as AMD's 2x-B200 HPC pitch: AMD's chart plots MI350X FP64 72.1 vs B200 SXM 5's 37.
